blogs.title: Is It Better to Read Code or Math Papers? Why Starting Your AI's Training with Code Might Be Key
blogs.description: This post explores the surprising finding that initializing a model with code training before moving to math might be more effective than just feeding it abstract mathematical papers. We break down why 'general' science data (like arXiv papers) isn't enough and how teaching a model to write programs helps it actually *solve* math problems.

blogs.title: Mining the Web Like Gold: How We Built a 120 Billion Token Math Dataset from Public Pages
blogs.description: Forget expensive private databases. Learn the clever engineering trick used to scrape Common Crawl (publicly available internet data) and filter out billions of irrelevant pages to create a massive, high-quality corpus of math problems. Perfect for anyone interested in data mining pipelines and scaling machine learning.

blogs.title: The Lazy Genius of GRPO: A New Reinforcement Learning Method That Skips the Expensive Critic Model
blogs.description: Reinforcement Learning (RL) is powerful but often too resource-heavy for modern AI. Introduce Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), a streamlined version of PPO that eliminates the need for a separate, heavy 'critic' model. Explain how calculating feedback internally saves memory while pushing open-source models closer to expert-level performance.
